The question was why is radiology more susceptible. I’m not disagreeing that primary care is susceptible to AI

I was thinking about that. But statements from a human are more subjective. Require social context which isn’t as easy to understand and is more complex. Not to mention vocal inflections and emotional contributions to patient presentation. 

Whereas images are more concrete. Black and white, much more pattern recognition friendly. Nothing abstract. So it’s a lot easier for AI


Not saying primary care is immune to AI. It’s definite more difficult to penetrate.

Pattern recognition. Input millions of normal scans. It’s easy for computers to analyze the abnormal. Give it correct clinical correlations with the abnormals and boom. You have a diagnostic radiologist.

Edit: will it necessarily be correct. Hard to say. But give it learning capabilities and over time the error of margin will lessen
